soundness_flags.label: Theorem 5, power conclusion
soundness_flags.one_line: With Psi_n=1{hat-gamma_pq>w_n}, the asserted band yields only hat-gamma_pq>=w_n when gamma_pq=2w_n, so it does not imply rejection or power at the stated weak boundary.

soundness_flags.label: Definition regularized-hessian-estimator and Theorem 5
soundness_flags.one_line: The “fixed positive fallback outside its regularity event” does not define either the event or the fallback density, so the empirical Monge--Ampere solution and reported statistic are not fully specified measurable objects.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 7
soundness_flags.one_line: A terminating procedure returning validated enclosures for the unknown population maps F_p,F_q has no stated computational input model, interval oracle, or estimator-to-population enclosure from which those validations can be computed.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 6
soundness_flags.one_line: Its upper bound depends on Theorem 5, which is explicitly conditional on an affirmative endpoint-response result, but Theorem 6 omits that condition and states an unconditional two-sided rate.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 4 and Theorem 5
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The boundary-uniform Hessian response and quadratic nonlinear remainder are open analytic inputs, not established premises.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Theorem 5 is acceptable only conditionally: if Open-ended Question 4 is resolved affirmatively, the specified simultaneous band follows; every downstream use of its upper bound, including Theorem 6, must carry that condition unless supplied an independent proof.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states that there is no explicit/precise characterization of SCMs producing cyclically monotone counterfactual maps and calls for a more general result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Appendix B.2, Theorem B.11, pp.21-22, equations (72)-(86)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem B.11 explicitly asserts strict Euclidean monotonicity of the counterfactual map; its displayed proof changes to an x-dependent weighted inner product in equation (84) before concluding the Euclidean claim.
The paper studies pointwise CLTs for smooth plug-in Brenier maps on a flat torus and reports a negative global L2 weak-convergence result in sufficiently high dimension.
The paper establishes near-minimax smooth optimal-map estimation through a semidual wavelet estimator and a complementary minimax lower bound.

Theorem 1.3 gives global C1,alpha map stability under Hölder conditions, while Theorem 1.5 supplies differentiable conormal divergence-form linear response; neither stated theorem supplies the proposed L-infinity-to-Hessian logarithmic endpoint modulus.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair the inferential boundary exactly: either define Psi_n with >=, or state power only for gamma_pq>2w_n (or gamma_pq>=(2+eta)w_n), then propagate the affirmative endpoint-response condition into every upper-bound theorem.

Specify a deterministic positivity-preserving fallback, the regularity event, and the numerical/interval-oracle model needed for the finite negative chord certificate; state the certificate only relative to those inputs.

Give the fixed-support least-favorable perturbation route explicitly and state whether its upper half is conditional on the endpoint-response OEQ; this would turn the lower-bound contribution into a clean matched testing frontier.

recommended_next_step: Return to Stage -1 for statement-level repair and re-review; the strict test-boundary error is load-bearing, while the structural and statistical novelty kernel remains plausible after correction.
